description: REQ-008 step 6's self-heal confirmation rule ('IF new_hrefs has EXACTLY ONE element, treat as now-confirmed... post_url = new_hrefs[0]') recreates, via a different code path, the EXACT false-positive-misattribution bug class this entire feature exists to eliminate (per the Context section's own incident narrative). The sidecar's `before_hrefs` baseline is captured ONCE, at original move-time, and per step 2 is explicitly NEVER updated in content ('with NO change to its content') across however many subsequent wakes the clip stays stuck in $CLIP_PENDING_VERIFY. Meanwhile REQ-008 step 1 explicitly guarantees the independent new-content pipeline keeps posting OTHER clips every wake regardless ('does NOT block that wake's normal new-content posting pipeline'), and run.sh (confirmed at /Users/anicca/anicca/skills/earn/clip/run.sh:41-105) posts up to one new clip per wake unconditionally today. Concrete trace: wake N, clip1 fails to confirm its own post (genuinely never published), moves to pending-verify with sidecar={P1..P5}. Wake N+1: self-heal(clip1) runs first (current reels still {P1..P5}) -> inconclusive, mtime touched. Same wake N+1, AFTER self-heal, the new-content pipeline successfully posts an UNRELATED clip2 -> account now {P1..P5,Q2}. Wake N+2: only clip1 is pending (or it is again the oldest per round-robin); self-heal(clip1) computes new_hrefs = {P1..P5,Q2} - {P1..P5} = {Q2} -- EXACTLY ONE element -> the spec's own rule classifies this as 'now-confirmed', moves clip1 to $CLIP_POSTED, deletes its sidecar, and writes a ledger line with status:'posted', post_url = clip2's real URL Q2 -- even though clip1 itself was NEVER actually published. This silently and permanently (a) mis-attributes clip2's post to clip1 in the ledger and (b) causes clip1's own video to be dropped from ever being retried (moved out of pending-verify, sidecar gone) despite never having landed on Instagram -- a duplicated-attribution + silent-data-loss bug, exactly the class of error the 2026-07-03 incident (described in behavioral-spec.md's own Context section) already burned the team on. The spec's mitigating text ('Documented known limitation... if new content keeps landing... on EVERY subsequent wake, new_hrefs could keep having >1 element indefinitely... This is SAFE') is factually wrong: it only analyzes the >=2-unrelated-posts case (correctly deferred as ambiguous) and never analyzes the much more likely exactly-1-unrelated-post case, which sails through as a false 'published' classification. The spec also underscopes the collision window to 'the SAME wake's independent new-content pipeline' (REQ-008 step 6, behavioral-spec.md:209-210), when the real risk spans ANY subsequent wake up until the stuck clip resolves, since the sidecar baseline is frozen at original move-time, not refreshed per-check.

evidence.snippet: new_hrefs = stabilized_reels_set - set(sidecar_hrefs). IF new_hrefs has EXACTLY ONE element, THE SYSTEM SHALL treat it as now-confirmed... Documented known limitation... if new content keeps landing... on EVERY subsequent wake, new_hrefs could keep having >1 element indefinitely... This is SAFE (never guesses, never duplicate-posts, never loses the clip)

corroboratingEvidence.description: confirms the new-content pipeline posts one new clip per wake unconditionally today, independent of any pending-verify state -- the mechanism that produces the unrelated Q2 href in the trace above
